top_story.headline: Census Bureau sole-sources $950,000 in voter registration data from Labels & Lists for 2027 test and 2030 Census planning
top_story.dek: The justification says Labels & Lists Inc. is the only company that can supply raw and enhanced voter registration records for all 50 states and the District of Columbia.
paragraphs: The U.S. Census Bureau, part of the U.S. Department of Commerce, plans a 12-month, firm-fixed-price contract with Labels & Lists Inc. (called L2 in the document) with no competition. The estimated value is $950,000, verified against the document. The Bureau wants four commercial data products: current and historical (from 2014) enhanced voter registration data, and current and historical (from 2012) raw state voter registration data, covering all 50 states and the District of Columbia.

According to the justification, the data would support the Bureau's administrative-records research, including matching people and addresses, the 2027 Census Test and the 2030 Census. It says L2 "is the only source capable of providing the specific data set for this unique requirement." It also says the Bureau "has historically utilized enhanced voter registration data supplied by L2." It cites a commercial-item authority (41 U.S.C. § 1901, as implemented by the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul) rather than a standard only-one-source finding.
USAspending's earliest federal contract on record under the vendor's name is dated October 23, 2026, four days before this notice was posted.

sections.headline: Architect of the Capitol extends proposals for a management capacity study to November 6
paragraphs: Three new items are tagged to the District: one sole-source justification and two solicitations. Five other tagged items were left out, either because an earlier edition already listed them (a Library of Congress-area award, a Defense Information Systems Agency circuit award, a Navy industry day and a Veterans Affairs sources-sought notice) or because the work is in Maryland (Suitland and Annapolis).

blocks.title: Architect of the Capitol extends the deadline on its management capacity study to November 6
blocks.text: Architect of the Capitol, the agency that maintains the Capitol campus, issued Amendment 01 to its Management Capacity Study solicitation, which answers vendor questions and pushes the proposal due date to November 6, 2026. The notice gives no value or scope beyond the project name. Seven attached files are queued for a later edition and have not been read.

blocks.title: Library of Congress seeks laundry and linen service for the VIP receptions and ceremonies of its Events Office
blocks.text: The Library of Congress wants a contractor to launder and deliver linens, uniforms and other textiles for its Library Events Office, which supports official events, public programs, ceremonies, receptions and VIP functions. The contractor would also keep inventory of the government-owned items. No value is posted, and five attached files are queued for a later edition.
Also worth a look

sections.headline: Air Force pays $1.5 million for Arbinger Institute leadership training with no competition

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Air Force pays $1.5 million for The Arbinger Institute's "outward mindset" training for 900 Hill Air Force Base leaders without competition
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Air Force wants a five-year blanket purchase agreement (about February 2027 to February 2032) with The Arbinger Institute for proprietary leadership courses for about 900 leaders at the Ogden Air Logistics Complex and two remote units. The justification says Arbinger is the sole source of its courseware. It also says the complex earlier had its own staff teach courses modeled on Arbinger's concept. Its cost line reads $1,500,000 including options, yet the same document describes a $3 million total ceiling. It was posted as a Special Notice.

meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: Defense Logistics Agency Energy bought petroleum products for Western Pacific military locations in three spot buys from BP Products North America Inc. The justification says the contracts were awarded May 1, 2026, and the paperwork was approved and published after award because preparing it first would have delayed the buy. It says BP's Cherry Point Refinery was the only offeror able to meet the delivery window. The notices were posted October 26, and the values are redacted.

blocks.title: State Department sole-sources event support for a high-level visit to Samarkand, Uzbekistan, to a state-run venue operator

sections.headline: Federal Bureau of Prisons extends Naphcare's Brooklyn jail medical contract while a protest holds up the new award
paragraphs: Seven new extensions or bridges today, three of them written up here. Two are tied to protests of the contracts they bridge.

blocks.title: Federal Bureau of Prisons keeps Naphcare on as medical provider at Metropolitan Detention Center Brooklyn for October at $889,018 while a protest holds up the new contract
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The justification covers October 1-31, 2026 and says the competitive contract is "pending the resolution of a protest." Naphcare would continue at its prior rates through monthly purchase orders. The Bureau of Prisons says Naphcare has served the institution for over five years, and that a new provider would need 30 or more days for credentialing and 30 to 60 days for security clearance. The pipeline logged one earlier Bureau of Prisons justification for Naphcare ($555,000, Federal Correctional Complex Petersburg).

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs hands VetPride Services a sole-source valet parking bridge at Providence after a protest killed the new award
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: Department of Veterans Affairs awarded contract 36C24127P0001 on July 30, 2026. A Government Accountability Office protest (B-424728.1) was filed August 7, and the agency terminated the award and promised corrective action. The Government Accountability Office dismissed the protest September 14. The bridge to incumbent VetPride Services, LLC was awarded October 1 as three months plus a three-month option, with up to six more months of extension.

blocks.title: NASA keeps United Rental's modular trailer at Kennedy Space Center for another year without competition, citing Artemis III pad work
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: National Aeronautics and Space Administration says the contractor capability that used to provide this facility is being removed as it realigns contracts with the Administration's direction. The trailer houses the team doing launch damage refurbishment of the launch pad for Artemis III. The 12-month United Rental lease starts October 1, 2026, though the document's end date reads September 30, 2026. NASA says it intends to compete the capability at the end of the year.

sections.headline: 145 agency and program spend plans approved; Title X funds held pending civil rights investigation
paragraphs: The federal government approved 145 new spend plans across dozens of agencies for fiscal years 2025 and 2026, covering routine allocations for benefits programs, law enforcement training, international development, and research initiatives. Three items stand out: a Title X family planning hold affecting 13 grantees, a $285 million apprenticeship expansion, and State Department rescissions.

blocks.text: Title X Family Planning Hold

U.S. Department of Health and Human Services is holding approximately $19.1 million in Title X family planning funding for 13 grant recipients pending an investigation into civil rights violations and active litigation (NPFRHA v. Kennedy). The withheld recipients are Virginia League for Planned Parenthood ($4,802,042), Planned Parenthood of Greater Texas ($2,133,365), Planned Parenthood of Minnesota, North Dakota, and South Dakota ($2,664,525), Planned Parenthood Association of Utah ($2,081,656), Planned Parenthood of Greater Ohio ($1,850,361), Planned Parenthood of Southern New England ($1,748,590), Planned Parenthood Great Northwest, Hawaii, Alaska, Indiana, and Kentucky (Alaska, $925,349; Indiana, $501,813; Kentucky, $438,148; Idaho, $482,976), Planned Parenthood of Northern New England ($464,894), Planned Parenthood South Atlantic (South Carolina, $527,325; North Carolina, $441,967). Spend plan.
Apprenticeship Expansion

U.S. Department of Labor will administer $285 million appropriated under the Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act of 2025 (P.L. 119-4) to expand registered apprenticeships under the National Apprenticeship Act. The funds, available from July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025, will support grants, cooperative agreements, and contracts with states, equity intermediaries, and business and labor partners to expand opportunities in skilled trades. Spend plan.
State Department Rescissions

U.S. Department of State's Cultural and International Protocol Affairs (CIPA) account is subject to multiple rescissions totaling $753,768: $203,328 from FY 2024–2025 carryover funds, $157,906 from FY 2025 appropriations, and $392,534 proposed for rescission in the President's special message. The account's total appropriated and carryforward funds for the period are $683,704. Spend plan.

Also apportioned (routine, non-flagged): Corps of Engineers—Civil Works, $55,909,000 (FY 2027 Expenses); U.S. Department of Agriculture, Office of the Secretary, $6,253,947,428 (FY 2027) and Rural Development, $512,279,500 (FY 2027 Salaries and Expenses); Executive Office of the President, Unanticipated Needs, $0 (FY 2027 Spectrum Relocation Fund).
